unit: Anne Shirley arrives in Avonlea on Prince Edward Island after being mistakenly brought from an orphan asylum by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, who had intended to adopt a boy. Despite initial intentions to send her back, Marilla and Matthew decide to keep her at Green Gables. Anne quickly makes a bosom friend in Diana Barry and enters Avonlea school, where an incident involving Gilbert Blythe calling her 'Carrots' starts a long-standing academic rivalry and grudge. Over the next few years, Anne gets into various humorous mishaps, such as inadvertently getting Diana intoxicated on currant wine, accidentally dyeing her hair green, and falling off a roof on a dare. Her resourcefulness shines when she saves Diana's little sister Minnie May from croup. She joins the Queen's Academy class, earns her teacher's license in one year, and wins the prestigious Avery Scholarship. However, after Matthew suddenly dies of a heart attack and Marilla faces failing eyesight, Anne selflessly gives up her college scholarship to stay at Green Gables, taking the Avonlea schoolteaching position instead. She helps found the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, helps raise the Keith twins, and finally reconciles her long-standing feud with Gilbert Blythe, becoming close friends as they both prepare for their futures.

label: History
value: Matthew insisted Anne be allowed to attend social events.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived a quiet, secluded life farming Green Gables with his sister Marilla. Reaching the age of sixty and suffering from heart trouble, he agreed with Marilla to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia to assist with farm work. When Matthew drove to Bright River station to collect the child, he was met by Anne Shirley instead, whom he lacked the heart to turn away. During the drive home, he was instantly charmed by her imaginative chatter and convinced Marilla to let her stay at Green Gables. Over the next four years, Matthew became Anne's steadfast champion and 'kindred spirit,' frequently indulging her wishes, buying her chocolate sweeties, insisting she be allowed to attend social events, and purchasing a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for her Christmas gift. He took immense pride in her academic achievements, encouraging her dreams and assuring her he was prouder of her than a dozen boys. In her second year of teaching, when Anne passed her entrance examinations to Queen's Academy at the top of the Island, Matthew expressed his deep pride in her. Shortly after her graduation, Matthew received a newspaper reporting the sudden collapse of the Abbey Bank where all his and Marilla's savings were kept; the shock caused an instantaneous, fatal heart attack in the doorway of Green Gables.

Following a severe quarrel over the parrot during a visit from local ministers, Emily left him, and Mr. Harrison subsequently relocated to Avonlea, buying Robert Bell's farm and living as an eccentric, self-proclaimed bachelor. He first met Anne Shirley when her Jersey cow repeatedly broke into his oatfield, leading to an angry confrontation. Shortly afterward, Anne accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's Jersey cow instead of her own, but when she went to confess and make amends, he forgave her good-naturedly and accepted her cow in exchange, sparking a warm neighborly friendship between them. Mr. Harrison supported Anne's Village Improvement Society projects, though he initially refused to contribute financially.

Though initially determined to return her, Marilla yielded to Matthew's wishes and agreed to raise the girl. When Matthew died suddenly of a heart attack following a bank failure, Marilla faced the prospect of selling Green Gables due to failing health and threatened blindness. However, Anne sacrificed her college scholarship to remain in Avonlea to teach and care for Marilla. Shortly after, Diana accidentally became intoxicated at Green Gables when Anne unknowingly served her currant wine instead of raspberry cordial, causing Mrs. Barry to strictly forbid Diana from playing with Anne. However, when her little sister Minnie May fell gravely ill with croup during her parents' absence, Anne saved the child's life, prompting Mrs. Barry to forgive Anne and restore the girls' friendship. Together with Anne, Diana joined the Avonlea school, participated in schoolhouse plays, the Debating Club concert, and the story club, and helped found the Avonlea Village Improvement Society as its treasurer. During their late teens, Diana became romantically involved with Fred Wright, eventually becoming engaged to him.

Later, Anne brought Stephen's son, Paul Irving, to visit Miss Lavendar, which eventually led to Stephen Irving returning to see her. unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet, solitary life at Green Gables with her shy brother Matthew. Deciding to adopt an orphan boy to assist Matthew on the farm, they were mistakenly sent an eleven-year-old girl named Anne Shirley. Though initially determined to return her, Marilla yielded to Matthew's wishes and agreed to raise the girl. Over the following years, Marilla conscientiously undertook Anne's upbringing, striving to correct her impulsive daydreams while gradually coming to love her as her own flesh and blood. When Matthew died suddenly of a heart attack following a bank failure, Marilla faced the prospect of selling Green Gables due to failing health and threatened blindness. However, Anne sacrificed her college scholarship to remain in Avonlea to teach and care for Marilla. To make the arrangement sustainable, Marilla invited her newly widowed friend, Rachel Lynde, to move into Green Gables, allowing Anne to pursue her college degree at Redmond while Marilla remained supported at home.
